item.title: Microsoft is openly competing with OpenAI, Anthropic more than ever
item.description: Microsoft pitched its own homegrown AI models, harnesses, and even a Mythos competitor on Wednesday, telling Wall Street it plans for continued growth.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg predicts that billions of people will have personal AI agents in five years
item.description: As Meta pours billions into AI infrastructure and agents, Zuckerberg is working to convince investors that the payoff will be worth the price.

item.title: Microsoft logs $3.2B from Anthropic investment, but OpenAI was a mixed bag
item.description: When Microsoft reported killer fourth-quarter earnings for its fiscal 2026 year (which ended June 30), it tucked in an interesting little tidbit about how its investments in the two biggest, and competing, AI labs are doing.

item.title: Zuckerberg says Meta’s enterprise AI opportunity extends beyond agents
item.description: On the company’s second-quarter earnings call Wednesday, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta sees a “large enterprise opportunity” spanning AI agents, APIs, compute, and internal software.

item.title: Discover what’s next for AI, from the SaaS reckoning to the agent security gap, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
item.description: At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, the AI Stage is back to dig into the single hottest topic in the community for the past few years, presented by Google for Startups.

item.title: Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng left the company citing health reasons, then joined OpenAI
item.description: Weng previously served as the VP of AI Safety Research at OpenAI.

item.title: The Hugging Face AI break-in, as told through an increasingly committed bear metaphor
item.description: Another way to think about the whole thing is to picture a bear at a campsite. (Really, we are going there.)

item.title: Claude Opus 5 became downright ruthless when tasked with running a vending machine
item.description: Andon Labs' latest vending machine simulation shows Opus 5 lied and colluded its way to become the best AI capitalist ever.

item.title: Hint, a new AI startup co-founded by Martha Stewart, offers an AI assistant for homeowners
item.description: AI home management startup Hint, co-founded by Martha Stewart, wants to become an “AI for your home,” combining property records, maintenance schedules, home documents, and an AI assistant into a single app.

item.title: Encore AI raises $30M to build AI agents that learn from customer calls
item.description: The startup analyzes calls, messages, and CRM data to identify effective sales techniques and turn them into playbooks for AI agents.

item.title: As AI content floods the internet, Pangram raises $9M to detect it
item.description: Pangram has raised $9 million to scale its AI detection software. The startup has also released a new AI text detection model, Pangram 4, and an AI image detection model in research preview.

item.title: Cyera agrees to acquire Oasis Security for $1B to safeguard proliferating AI agents
item.description: The deal is Cyera's third acquisition this year.

item.title: Bot-detection startup Spur nabs $200M from Insight
item.description: Spur Intelligence has raised a $200 million round from Insight Partners for its tech that can identify legit human traffic from bots.

item.title: MCP startup Runlayer accuses Rippling of stealing its product idea
item.description: Runlayer is suing Rippling after Rippling evaluated the startup's MCP gateway product and then opted to build one itself.

item.title: Sam Altman is ready to decelerate
item.description: His change of position comes after "the first security incident that I have felt very viscerally."

item.title: Data centers may face temporary power cuts to prevent blackouts on largest US grid
item.description: The decision arrives as the breakneck pace of data center construction has grid operators scrambling to generate power.

item.title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
item.description: Since launching last year, the startup today has more than 8 million people using the open source or hosted version of its models, and now generates annual recurring revenue of $21 million.

item.title: Recursive Superintelligence signs $410M compute deal with Amazon
item.description: Recursive’s emphasis on self-improving AI systems means much of the budget that would traditionally go toward headcount and operations is put straight into compute, as the company seeks to automate its own product development process.

item.title: Cursor makes its biggest India push yet ahead of SpaceX acquisition with localized pricing
item.description: Cursor says India is now its third-largest market globally and plans to expand local hiring and enterprise sales.

item.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei responds: doesn’t oppose open-weight models, but fears Chinese AI
item.description: Anthropic founder and CEO Dario Amodei made his views clear about open-weight models and China's growing AI capabilities.
